summary: Remote-controlled shell and PTY driven by WebSocket notifications from ai-support-agent.com
details: @ai-support-agent/cli ships a daemon (`ai-support-agent start`) that, once the operator authenticates, subscribes to AppSync WebSocket notifications from api.ai-support-agent.com / app.ai-support-agent.com and dispatches incoming messages to two shell surfaces on the installer's host. In shell-executor.js, `AGENT_COMMAND` payloads of type `execute_command` reach `executeShellCommand`, which invokes `spawn('/bin/sh', ['-c', command])` (or `cmd.exe /c` on Windows) with the command string taken from the remote payload. In terminal-session.js, `TerminalWebSocket` writes incoming WebSocket bytes into a node-pty-spawned interactive shell (`pty.spawn(spawnFile, spawnArgs,...)`, typically `/bin/bash`, `$SHELL`, or a tmux wrapper) via `this.ptyProcess.write(data)`. Once the daemon is running, anyone with the requisite API/tenant access at ai-support-agent.com can issue commands that execute arbitrary shell/PTY input as the installer user, providing full-host interactive RCE and persistence for as long as the daemon is running.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
